<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The play tells the story of Candracūḍa, a brave and virtuous Prince who is unjustly accused of a crime and banished from his kingdom. He eventually finds refuge in the forest, where he falls in love with the beautiful princess Rupavatī. However, their love is threatened by the machinations of Rupavatī's jealous stepmother, who plots to destroy their happiness and turn Rupavatī against Candracūḍa. The play explores themes of love, loyalty, betrayal, and the struggle for justice and redemption, and features complex characters, poetic language, and dramatic plot twists. It is considered a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature and continues to be studied and performed to this day.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Candracūḍa is a five-act play that tells the story of the eponymous hero, Prince Candracūḍa, who is falsely accused of stealing the queen's jewellery and banished from his kingdom. He seeks refuge in the forest, where he meets and falls in love with Princess Rupavatī. However, Rupavatī's stepmother, Queen Ratnaprabhā, is jealous of their love and plots to destroy it by turning Rupavatī against Candracūḍa. Meanwhile, a group of bandits led by the notorious Dhanavāhana are causing havoc in the kingdom, and the King and his ministers are struggling to deal with the situation. As the play unfolds, Candracūḍa must overcome a series of obstacles and challenges to clear his name, win the love of Rupavatī, and restore order to the kingdom. The play features a diverse cast of characters, including warriors, scholars, ministers, bandits, and gods, and explores themes such as love, loyalty, betrayal, justice, and redemption.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Candracūḍa is a unique work of Sanskrit literature due to its complex characters, intricate plot, and poetic language. It blends elements of romance, adventure, and political intrigue to create a rich and multi-layered narrative that engages the reader on multiple levels. The play is notable for its exploration of themes such as love, loyalty, and justice, as well as its vivid portrayal of Indian society and culture during the 12th century. Additionally, the play's use of vivid imagery, metaphor, and wordplay showcases the mastery of Sanskrit poetic language, making it a valuable and enduring contribution to the canon of Indian literature.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Candracūḍa is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature due to its innovative approach to storytelling, use of poetic language, and exploration of enduring themes. The play reflects the social and cultural milieu of 12th-century India, while also presenting a timeless tale of love, betrayal, and redemption. Its complex characters and intricate plot demonstrate the range and versatility of Sanskrit dramatic literature, while its poetic language and imagery showcase the richness and beauty of the Sanskrit language.</div></div></div>
